title: Concrete reference templates for web API + CLI LLM patterns
creator: Maya Singh
description: Provide a set of opinionated, runnable reference templates that demonstrate robust LLM integration patterns across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), Go (simple HTTP server) and a CLI example. Focus areas: ergonomic streaming APIs, best-practice retry/backoff configurations, graceful cancellation and backpressure handling, and pragmatic examples of batching + prefix/KV caching. These templates should be small (single repo per template), documented, and accompanied by a short cookbook note describing trade-offs and when to pick each pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Four repositories (or monorepo packages): nextjs-web-chat, fastapi-stream-api, go-llm-server, cli-assistant. Each has a README with setup and a one-command run.
Streaming examples show both server->client and client->server streaming patterns with pause/resume or chunked rendering in the UI/CLI.
Retry behavior documented and implemented: idempotency guidelines, exponential backoff with jitter, and circuit-breaker note for synchronous endpoints.

Example shows how to wire Redwood SDK batching and prefix/KV cache endpoints with minimal config and a noted benchmark of per-token latency and cost for a 1k concurrent chatbot workload (approx numbers).
PRs merged for all templates, CI green, and a short demo video (2-3 minutes) recorded and linked in the ticket.
notes: We want examples that are copy/paste friendly for product teams evaluating Redwood. Avoid large frameworks beyond Next.js/FastAPI; keep runtime footprint small. Focus on clear ergonomics: streaming iterators in Python, async generators in TS, and a lightweight channel-based reader in Go.
tradeoffs: Simpler helper wrappers vs exposing raw streaming WebSocket/event-stream: wrappers improve ergonomics but can hide backpressure — include both approaches in the FastAPI/Next.js examples to demonstrate trade-offs.

Bundling all templates into one monorepo simplifies CI but increases cognitive load for consumers. We will adopt a hybrid: single repo with clear package folders and independent package.json/go.mod/pyproject for each template.
Demonstrate retries at the SDK layer (recommended) and at a small API gateway retry shim (optional). Emphasize idempotency keys for mutable operations.
Keep the CLI synchronous by default but provide an opt-in streaming mode for interactive sessions; mention when synchronous is preferable (batch jobs, reproducible outputs).
